symptoms: Leaves show a normal green color, clean margins, and proper turgor pressure.
No necrotic spots, powdery growth, mold, or visual signs of pest damage.
causes: Optimal soil nutrients and moisture levels.
Effective preventative pest management and clean farming practices.
organic_treatment: Continue organic composting and bio-fertilizer application to maintain soil microbiology.
fertilizer: Apply balanced N-P-K organic compost or vermicompost as per growth requirements.
Use micronutrient spray (Zinc, Boron) if minor soil deficiencies are observed.
prevention: Use drip irrigation to keep foliage dry and reduce spore germination risks.
farmer_tips: Ensure adequate spacing between plants to maximize sunlight exposure.
Perform soil tests annually to keep nutrient ratios balanced.

symptoms: Large, dark, water-soaked leaf lesions that expand rapidly and turn paper-thin.
White, velvety fungal growth on leaf undersides in wet weather.
Large, greasy, chocolate-brown, firm patches on green or ripe tomatoes.
causes: Oomycete pathogen overwintering on potato tubers or volunteer solanaceous hosts.
Wet, cool summer weather allowing explosive spore production.
organic_treatment: Destroy infected plants immediately (bag and bury them; do not compost).
Apply copper fungicides frequently during cool, wet weather forecasts.
chemical_treatment: Spray oomycide-specific fungicides like Mefenoxam or Chlorothalonil.
fertilizer: Avoid high nitrogen; keep plants robust with balanced nutrients.
prevention: Plant resistant tomato cultivars (e.g., Mountain Merit, Defiant PHR, Iron Lady).
Prune canopy to promote rapid drying.
farmer_tips: If late blight is in your area and the forecast shows rain and fog with cool temperatures, spray protective fungicides immediately. Do not wait for symptoms.
gemini_prompt_context.weather: Cool, wet, rainy, and foggy conditions (10-21°C) with 90%+ humidity.
